# Correcting records 78 and 81, and the two halves of the disclosure I gave only one of

The sixth review returned this ticket on four findings and every one is about what I wrote rather than what the
code does. The code it checked and could not break: the fifth review's scenario is refused by name in both
directions, the guards hold, and the decision that re-citing a red beside a different green is never legitimate
was verified structurally rather than accepted, because `advance` moves forward only and every path back to tdd
increments the attempt, so a corrected green always belongs to a later attempt.

**The failure reason in record 81 is wrong, and record 78 is wrong the same way.** Both say the sixth failure of
the RED was a `ValueError: substring not found`. Record 76's own captured output says
`AssertionError: shadow not found in the route of the position its entry declares`. The review reproduced it by
replacing `gates.py` with the pre-fix revision and got exactly six failures, five `HarnessError not raised` and
one `AssertionError`, no `ValueError`. The two mean different defects: a `ValueError` from an index call would
mean the route clause was absent from the docstring altogether, while the `AssertionError` means it was present
and unqualified, which is the defect F3 of the fifth review was actually about. I took the wording from the
implementing round's report without reading it against the stored output, which is the check a failure reason
exists to survive. Record 81 is accepted and the journal is append-only, so this record is the correction rather
than an edit.

**The disclosure of the `git add -A` consequence had two halves and I gave one.** I wrote that the commit whose
message describes the fourth review's return also carries the fix. The mirror is worse and I did not say it:
commit 34f2511, whose subject announces attempt 6's fix, carries **six journal records and no code at all**. The
diff between the return commit and it is empty outside the journal, so the whole production half, 231 inserted
lines in `harness/gates.py` plus `handoff.py` and three test files, sits in the commit whose subject says the
fourth review returns the ticket. Anyone tracing which commit introduced `_the_journal_puts_it_elsewhere` reads
the log, opens the commit named as the fix, and finds nothing of it there.

**The ordering in my safety argument is false.** Record 78 says the pair rule refuses a cross-attempt-split pair
"before the attribution is ever reached". It does not: `_require_the_pair_is_one_round` runs after the whole slice
loop, while `_the_journal_pairs_it_with_another_check` runs inside `cited_check` during it, so the new rule
refuses first and the split-pair sentence is the one a session does not see. The conclusion survives, because both
rules refuse and the case still cannot arise, but the net I said it rested on sits later in the path than I
claimed. The code's own docstring does not make that claim and is accurate; only my prose did.

**And the hedge I dropped.** Record 75 said the implementer's account of being blocked "was accurate for the
moment it was written", because at that moment the return did not yet exist. The Outcome compressed records 67
and 75 into one clause and stated a stage refusal as fact. Records 64, 65 and 66 are all in the journal at tdd
attempt 6, none refused, and no refusal is recorded anywhere in this repository. So the Outcome asserted something
the journal does not carry, which is the same verdict the fifth review reached about the same paragraph of the
same file, one round later. The hedge goes back.

Two residues the review judged rather than inherited, and left correctly open: within one attempt, before any
accepted record exists, a pairing rests on the citing record's word, which it verified is irreducible; and a
malformed position normalises to null, which is safe in the direction that matters because an unreadable position
falls to the plan's union, the wider and therefore stricter scope. It added one fact worth carrying: the real
reach of that conflation is the **absent** key rather than a malformed value, and 72 of the 103 slice entries in
this repository's journals have no `position` key at all, every one of them in a delivered ticket.
